title: GreenTree Hospitality Group Ltd. Reports Third Quarter of 2026 Financial Results
summary: Total revenues decreased by 22.2% year-over-year to RMB243.0 million (US$36.2 million)[1]. Net income was RMB49.3 million (US$7.3 million)[1] compared to RMB59.0 million for the third quarter of 2025.

-

- *Total revenues decreased by* *22.2* *%* *year* *-* *over* *-* *year to* *RMB* *243.0* *million* *(* *US$* *36.2* *million* *)* \[1\].
- *Net income was* *RMB* *49.3* *million (US$* *7.* *3* *million)* \[1\] *compared to RMB* *5* *9.0* *million* *for the* *third* *quarter of 202* *5* *.*
- *Core net income* \[3\] *was RMB55.4 million (US$8.3 million)* \[1\] *, compared to* *RMB78.6 million* *for the third quarter of 2025.*
- *Net cash provided by operating activities* *in* *creased* *29.1* *% year* *-* *over* *-* *year to RMB* *186.5* *million (US$* *27.8* *million* *)* \[1\] *.*


SHANGHAI


, Nov. 20, 2026


/[PRNewswire](http://www.prnewswire.com/) / -- GreenTree Hospitality Group Ltd. (NYSE: GHG) ("GreenTree", the "Company", "we", "us" and "our"), a leading hospitality and restaurant management group in China, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter of 2026.


**Third Quarter of** **202** **6** **Operational Highlights**


**Hotels**


- A total of 4,651 hotels with 333,590 hotel rooms were in operation as of September 30, 2026.
- The Company opened 59 hotels in the third quarter of 2026 and had a pipeline of 1,313 hotels contracted for or under development as of September 30, 2026.
- The average daily room rate was RMB165, a decrease of 5.0% from RMB173 in the third quarter of 2025.
- The occupancy rate was 68.1%, decreased from 71.3% in the third quarter of 2025.
- Revenue per available room, or RevPAR, was RMB112, a 9.3% year-over-year decrease.


**Restaurants**


- A total of 203 restaurants were in operation as of September 30, 2026.
- The AC (average check) was RMB37, a 1.6% year-over-year decrease.
- The ADT (average daily tickets) was 62, decreased from 100 in the third quarter of 2025.
- The ADS (average daily sales per store) was RMB2,280, a decrease of 38.6% from RMB3,714 in the third quarter of 2025.


\[1\] The conversion of Renminbi ("RMB") into United States dollars ("US$") is based on the exchange rate of 6.7045 on September 30, 2026 as set forth in H.10 statistical release of the U.S. Federal Reserve Board and available at[https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h10/20261005/](https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h10/20261005/) . No representation is made that the RMB amounts could have been, or could be, converted into US$ at such rate or at any other rate.


\[2\] Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP) is calculated as net income plus other operating expenses, income tax expense, share of loss in equity investees, net of tax, interest expense, depreciation and amortization, losses from investment in equity securities, other general expenses, and other expense, net, but excludes other operating income, interest income and other, net, gains from investment in equity securities, share of gains in equity investees (net of tax), and other income, net. The calculation of Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP) included in this report has been aligned according to the above mentioned definition.


\[3\] Core net income (non-GAAP) is calculated as net income plus share-based compensation, losses from investments in equity securities (net of 25% tax), other expense (net of 25% tax), one-time fees and expense, bad debt, income tax expenses related to dividend distribution, and other general expenses but excludes subsidies (net of 25% tax), gains from investment in equity securities (net of 25% tax), and other income (net of 25% tax).


\[4\] Each ADS represents one ordinary share.

**Total revenues** were RMB243.0 million (US$36.2 million)\[1\], a 22.2% year-over-year decrease.


Hotel revenues were RMB212.2 million (US$31.7 million)\[1\], a 19.3% year-over-year decrease due to a 9.3% year-over-year decrease in RevPAR and a net closure of 13 L&O hotels since the third quarter of 2025 due to lease expiration and strategic reviews. The decrease was partially offset by revenues from new openings.


Restaurant revenues were RMB30.8 million (US$4.6 million)\[1\], a 37.7% year-over-year decrease, mainly due to a 38.6% decrease in ADS and a net closure of 3 L&O stores since the third quarter of 2025 due to strategic reviews, offset by revenues from new F&M store openings.


Total revenues for the first nine months of 2026 were RMB705.9 million (US$105.3 million)\[1\], an 18.5% year-over-year decrease.


**Total revenues from leased-and-operated, or L&O, hotels** **and restaurants** were RMB100.8 million (US$15.0 million)\[1\], a 29.0% year-over-year decrease.


Total revenues from L&O hotels were RMB84.6 million (US$12.6 million)\[1\], a 26.8% year-over-year decrease. The decrease was primarily attributable to a 12.9% year-over-year decrease in the third quarter RevPAR of L&O hotels, a net closure of 13 L&O hotels since the third quarter of 2025, and the reduction in sublease revenues resulting from the closure of L&O hotels.


Total revenues from L&O restaurants were RMB16.2 million (US$2.4 million)\[1\], a 38.9% year-over-year decrease, mainly due to a net closure of 3 L&O stores and the year-over-year decrease of 16.2% in L&O stores' ADS.


Total revenues from L&O hotels and restaurants for the first nine months of 2026 were RMB291.2 million (US$43.4 million)\[1\], a 26.3% year-over-year decrease.


**Total revenues from franchised-and-managed, or F&M, hotels** **and restaurants** were RMB128.2 million (US$19.1 million)\[1\], a 14.0% year-over-year decrease.


Total revenues from F&M hotels were RMB127.0 million (US$18.9 million)\[1\], a 13.8% year-over-year decrease, primarily due to a 9.1% decrease in F&M hotels' RevPAR, an exemption of management fees for hotels facing business difficulties, and a decline of RMB4.5 million in membership revenues. Franchise fee revenue for 2026 reflects, in each quarter, reductions arising from fee waivers granted to franchisees. In 2025, the corresponding reductions were originally recognized in aggregate in the fourth quarter. To present the 2025 interim information on a basis consistent with 2026 and to enhance quarter-to-quarter comparability, the comparative quarterly figures for 2025 have been reclassified to allocate these reductions to the quarters in which the waivers were granted. The reallocation affects only the intra-year timing of recognition and has no impact on full-year 2025 revenue, net income, or any previously reported annual results.


The decrease in membership revenues was partially due to the amortization cycle started from the pandemic period three years ago, in which the sales of membership cards were historically under-performed.


Total revenues from F&M restaurants were RMB1.2 million (US$0.2 million)\[1\], a 35.2% year-over-year decrease, mainly due to a decrease of 38.2% in the ADS of F&M stores and an exemption of management fees.


Total revenues from F&M hotels and restaurants for the first nine months of 2026 were RMB370.2 million (US$55.2 million)\[1\], a 10.5% year-over-year decrease.


**Total revenues from** **wholesale and others** were RMB14.0 million (US$2.1 million)\[1\], a 33.6% year-over-year decrease, mainly due to the decline in the wholesale segment of the restaurant business.


Total revenues from wholesale and others for the first nine months of 2026 were RMB44.4 million (US$6.6 million)\[1\], a 23.0% year-over-year decrease.

**Operating costs** were RMB150.6 million (US$22.5 million)\[1\], a 20.4% year-over-year decrease.


Operating costs of the hotel business were RMB124.5 million (US$18.6 million)\[1\], a 14.9% year-over-year decrease. The decrease was mainly attributable to lower staff related costs, lower depreciation and amortization, and lower rental costs caused by the net closure of 13 L&O hotels since the third quarter of 2025. For comparability, the year-over-year change is presented on a basis that applies the same treatment of straight-line amortization of lease expense to the corresponding period of 2025; it affects only the intra-year allocation within 2025 and has no impact on full-year 2025 operating costs, net income or any previously reported annual results.


Operating costs of the restaurant business in the third quarter of 2026 were RMB26.1 million (US$3.9 million)\[1\], a 39.3% year-over-year decrease, due to the closure of L&O stores.


For the first nine months of 2026, operating costs were RMB455.9 million (US$68.0 million)\[1\], an 18.0% decrease.


**Selling and marketing expenses** were RMB12.9 million (US$1.9 million)\[1\], a 4.4% year-over-year decrease.


Selling and marketing expenses of the hotel business were RMB10.5 million (US$1.6 million)\[1\], a 6.8% year-over-year decrease. The decrease was mainly due to lower advertising and commission expenses.


Selling and marketing expenses of the restaurant business were RMB2.3 million (US$0.3 million)\[1\], an 8.1% year-over-year increase. The increase was mainly due to higher commission expenses.


For the first nine months of 2026, selling and marketing expenses were RMB34.5 million (US$5.1 million)\[1\], a 15.9% decrease.


**General and administrative, or G&A expenses** were RMB23.8 million (US$3.6 million)\[1\], a 7.5% year-over-year increase.


G&A expenses of the hotel business were RMB19.8 million (US$3.0 million)\[1\], a 1.0% year-over-year decrease.


The decrease was mainly due to lower G&A staff related expenses and office expenses. However, two major factors increased G&A expenses this quarter: first, higher professional fees, and second, expenses attributable to our market entry into Malaysia during the period, which had no comparable in the prior-year period.


On a comparable basis, excluding these two factors, G&A for the third quarter decreased 24.5% year over year.


G&A expenses of the restaurant business were RMB4.0 million (US$0.6 million)\[1\], an 85.3% year-over-year increase. The increase was primarily due to the one-time compensation paid to laid-off employees due to store closures.


General and administrative expenses for the first nine months of 2026 were RMB79.0 million (US$11.8 million)\[1\], a 25.5% year-over-year decrease.


**Other operating expenses** were RMB3.9 million (US$0.6 million)\[1\].
Other operating expenses for the first nine months of 2026 were RMB7.3 million (US$1.1 million)\[1\], decreased from RMB11.5 million one year ago.


**Other general expenses** were RMB10.5 million (US$1.6 million)\[1\], mainly attributable to provisions for franchisee loans.


Other general expenses for the first nine months of 2026 were RMB20.3 million (US$3.0 million)\[1\], a decrease from RMB31.1 million one year ago.


**Gross profit** was RMB92.4 million (US$13.8 million)\[1\], a year-over-year decrease of 25.0%. Gross margin was 38.0%, compared to 39.4% a year ago. The gross profit of the hotel business was RMB87.7 million (US$13.1 million)\[1\], a 24.9% year-over-year decrease. Gross margin of the hotel business was 41.3%, compared to 44.4% a year ago. The gross profit of the restaurant business was RMB4.7 million (US$0.7 million)\[1\], a 26.5% year-over-year decrease. Gross margin of the restaurant business was 15.2%, compared to 12.9% a year ago.


**Income from operations** in the third quarter of 2026 was RMB52.8 million (US$7.9 million)\[1\], compared to income from operations of RMB68.8 million in the third quarter of 2025, with a margin of 21.7%.


Income from operations of the hotel business was RMB54.4 million (US$8.1 million)\[1\], compared to an income from operations of RMB67.8 million in the third quarter of 2025, with a margin of 25.6%. On a comparable basis, excluding the factors mentioned above regarding G&A expenses, as well as revenues and costs attributable to our market entry into Malaysia, income from operations for the third quarter would be RMB57.4 million, a 15.3% year-over-year decrease.


Loss from operations of the restaurant business in the third quarter of 2026 was RMB1.6 million (US$0.2 million)\[1\], compared to income from operations of RMB0.9 million in the third quarter of 2025, with an operating loss margin of 5.2%. The loss was primarily due to the decline in revenues and one-time compensation for laid-off employees of closed stores.


Income from operations for the first nine months of 2026 was RMB129.7 million (US$19.3 million)\[1\] compared to income from operations of RMB139.2 million in the first nine months of 2025, with a margin of 18.4%, increased from 16.1% for the first nine months of 2025.


**Net income** in the third quarter of 2026 was RMB49.3 million (US$7.3 million)\[1\], compared to a net income of RMB59.0 million in the third quarter of 2025, and net margin was 20.3%.


Net income of the hotel business was RMB50.9 million (US$7.6 million)\[1\], including gains from investment in equity securities of RMB28.5 million and foreign exchange losses of RMB17.8 million, compared to a net income of RMB58.1 million in the third quarter of 2025, and net margin was 24.0%. On a comparable basis, excluding the factors mentioned above regarding G&A expenses, as well as revenues and costs attributable to our market entry into Malaysia,


net income for the third quarter would be RMB53.9 million, a 7.2% year-over-year decrease.


Net loss of the restaurant business in the third quarter of 2026 was RMB1.7 million (US$0.3 million)\[1\], compared to a net income of RMB0.9 million in the third quarter of 2025, and net loss margin was 5.5%.


Net income for the first nine months of 2026 was RMB84.5 million (US$12.6 million)\[1\], compared to a net income of RMB236.8 million in the first nine months of 2025


, and net margin was 12.0%. Net income for the first nine months of 2025 was contributed by the one-time divestment of our ownership in Argyle and fair value fluctuation in securities. Excluding these factors, net income for the first nine months of 2026 decreased 9.4% year over year.


**Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP)** \[2\] in the third quarter of 2026 was RMB81.2 million (US$12.1 million)\[1\], a year-over-year decrease of 28.6%. Adjusted EBITDA margin, defined as adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP)\[2\] as a percentage of total revenues, was 33.4%, compared to 36.4% a year ago.


Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP)\[2\] for the first nine months of 2026 was RMB203.2 million (US$30.3 million)\[1\], a year-over-year decrease of 16.2%.


**Core net income (non-GAAP)** \[3\] in the third quarter of 2026 was RMB55.4 million (US$8.3 million)\[1\], a year-over-year decrease of 29.5%. The core net margin, defined as core net income (non-GAAP)\[3\] as a percentage of total revenues, was 22.8%, compared to 25.2% one year ago.


Core net income (non-GAAP)\[3\] for the first nine months of 2026 was RMB133.2 million (US$19.9 million)\[1\], a year-over-year decrease of 18.6%.


**Earnings per American Depositary Share, or ADS** **\[4\]** **, (basic and diluted)** were RMB0.49 (US$0.07)\[1\], decreased from RMB0.59 one year ago.


**Earnings per American Depositary Share, or ADS** **\[4\]** **, (basic and diluted)** for the first nine months of 2026 were RMB0.85 (US$0.13)\[1\], decreased from RMB2.37 one year ago.


**Core net income per ADS** **\[4\]** **(basic and diluted) (non-GAAP)** was RMB0.55 (US$0.08)\[1\], decreased from RMB0.78 a year ago.


**Core net income per ADS** **\[4\]** **(basic and diluted) (non-GAAP)** was RMB1.32 (US$0.20)\[1\] for the first nine months of 2026, a decrease from RMB1.62 a year ago.


**Cash** **F** **low** **.** Operating cash inflow in the third quarter of 2026 was RMB186.5 million (US$27.8 million)\[1\] as a result of income from operations. The amount increased by RMB42.0 million compared with the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to a net decline in other receivable from franchisees and a net increase in accounts payable to franchisees. Investing cash outflow was RMB1,337.1 million (US$199.4 million)\[1\], primarily due to the purchase of the Yangpu Riverside property in Shanghai described under "Recent Developments." Financing cash inflow was RMB953.5 million (US$142.2 million)\[1\], mainly due to bank borrowings to fund that purchase.


**Cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash, short-term investments, investments in equity securities and time deposits.** As of September 30, 2026, the Company had total cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash, short term investments, investments in equity securities and time deposits of RMB1,794.3 million (US$267.6 million)\[1\], compared to RMB2,000.3 million as of June 30, 2026. The decrease was mainly due to the purchase of strategic assets along the Huangpu River waterfront in Yangpu District, partially offset by cash from operating activities.


**Guidance**


Based on our performance in the first nine months, we maintain our previous revenue guidance for the hotel business, that we expect revenue to decrease by 10% to 15%


year-over-year for the year of 2026. The guidance set forth above reflects the Company's current and preliminary views based on its operations and may not be indicative of the final financial results for any future periods or the full year.


**Recent Developments**


*Acquisition of Shanghai Yangpu Riverside Property*


In late August 2026, the Company took possession of a riverfront property in Yangpu District, Shanghai, which it acquired through a competitive bidding process for total consideration of approximately RMB1.31 billion.


The acquisition was funded primarily by long-term bank borrowings of approximately RMB917.0


million, on terms the Company considers favorable, with the balance already paid


from cash on hand. As of September 30, 2026, the Company held RMB1,794.3 million in cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash, short-term investments and time deposits.


The property has a total floor area of approximately 50,000 square meters and fronts the Huangpu River in the Yangpu Riverside area, one of Shanghai's main technology corridors and home to the regional headquarters of a number of leading internet platform and artificial intelligence companies. Riverfront properties of this scale in the area rarely come to market, and comparable space is generally unavailable for lease or available only at high rents.


The Company plans to convert the property into an upscale flagship hotel of approximately 360 rooms, together with a lifestyle and commercial center of approximately 20,000 square meters that will serve hotel guests and the surrounding business community. Conversion work is under way


, and the Company targets opening by the end of 2027.


The Company believes the acquisition price is well below the property's replacement cost and expects the project to generate attractive returns on its investment. The Company also expects the property to:


- serve as a showcase for its upscale hotel brand to franchisees and partners;
- house part of its corporate offices; and
- provide a venue for franchisee conferences and events, which the Company expects will reduce certain selling and marketing costs over time.


The Company remains committed to its franchise-led, asset-light model. This acquisition is a selective investment in a flagship asset intended to support the growth of its upscale franchise business, and it does not affect the share repurchase program described below.


*Acquisition of Kuala Lumpur Property*


In July 2026, the Company took possession of a hotel property located opposite the Petronas Twin Towers in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, which it agreed to acquire in 2025. The property will serve as the Company's flagship in Malaysia and as a base for expanding its hotel network across Southeast Asia.


**Share Repurchase Program**


The Board of Directors has approved a share repurchase program authorizing the Company to repurchase up to US$5 million of its Class A ordinary shares over a two-year period, effective from the date of approval. Repurchases may be conducted through open market transactions at prevailing market prices, privately negotiated transactions, block trades or other legally permitted methods, at the Company's discretion, subject to market conditions, applicable securities laws and regulations, and the trading price of the Company's ADSs.


As of November 18, 2026, the Company had repurchased 62,922 of its ADSs for an aggregate repurchase price of US$61,396.74. The Company plans to continue its ADS repurchases under the program (which has unutilized capacity of approximately US$4.94 million), subject to market conditions, applicable law (including Rule 10b-18) and the Company's insider trading policy. The program may be suspended, modified or terminated at any time at the Board's discretion without prior notice.


**Continued Listing Notice from NYSE**


The Company received a letter from the New York Stock Exchange (the "NYSE"), dated November 4, 2026, notifying the Company that it was not in compliance with applicable price criteria in the NYSE's continued listing standards because, as of November 3, 2026, the average closing price of the Company's American Depositary Shares (the "ADSs") was less than US$1.00 per ADS over a consecutive 30 trading-day period.


Pursuant to Section 802.01C of the NYSE's Listed Company Manual, the Company has six months (the "Cure Period") following receipt of the notice to regain compliance with the minimum share price requirement. The Company can regain compliance at any time during the Cure Period if on the last trading day of any calendar month during the Cure Period the Company has a closing share price of at least US$1.00 per ADS and an average closing share price of at least US$1.00 per ADS over the 30 trading-day period ending on the last trading day of that month. In the event that at the expiration of the Cure Period, both a US$1.00 per ADS closing share price on the last trading day of the Cure Period and a US$1.00 per ADS average closing share price over the 30 trading-day period ending on the last trading day of the Cure Period are not attained, the NYSE will commence suspension and delisting procedures.


The Company notified the NYSE on November 17, 2026 of its intent to cure the deficiency.


The Company is considering all available options to regain compliance with the NYSE's continued listing standards.


During the Cure Period, the Company's ADSs will continue to be listed and traded on the NYSE, subject to compliance with other NYSE continued listing standards and other rights of the NYSE to delist the ADSs. To the Company's knowledge, the Company is currently in compliance with all other NYSE continued listing standards. The NYSE notice does not affect the Company's business operations or its U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission reporting requirements.


**Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


We believe that Adjusted EBITDA and core net income, as we present them, are useful financial metrics to assess our operating and financial performance before the impact of investing and financing transactions, income taxes and certain non-core and non-recurring items in our financial statements.


The presentation of Adjusted EBITDA and core net income should not be construed as an indication that our future results will be unaffected by other charges and gains we consider to be outside the ordinary course of our business.


The use of Adjusted EBITDA and core net income has certain limitations because it does not reflect all items of income and expenses that affect our operations. Items excluded from Adjusted EBITDA and core net income are significant components in understanding and assessing our operating and financial performance. Depreciation and amortization expense for various long-term assets, income tax and share-based compensation have been and will be incurred and are not reflected in the presentation of Adjusted EBITDA. Each of these items should also be considered in the overall evaluation of our results. Additionally, Adjusted EBITDA and core net income do not consider capital expenditures and other investing activities and should not be considered as a measure of our liquidity. We compensate for these limitations by providing the relevant disclosure of our depreciation and amortization, interest expense/income, gains/losses from investments in equity securities, income tax expenses, share-based compensation, share of loss in equity investees, subsidies and other relevant items both in our reconciliations to the corresponding U.S. GAAP financial measures and in our consolidated financial statements, all of which should be considered when evaluating our performance.


The terms Adjusted EBITDA and core net income are not defined under U.S. GAAP, and Adjusted EBITDA and core net income are not measures of net income, operating income, operating performance or liquidity presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP. When assessing our operating and financial performance, you should not consider this data in isolation or as a substitute for our net income, operating income or any other operating performance measure that is calculated in accordance with U.S. GAAP. In addition, our Adjusted EBITDA and core net income may not be comparable to Adjusted EBITDA and core net income or similarly titled measures utilized by other companies since such other companies may not calculate Adjusted EBITDA and core net income in the same manner as we do.


Reconciliations of the Company's non-GAAP financial measures, including Adjusted EBITDA and core net income, to the consolidated statement of operations information are included at the end of this press release.


**About GreenTree Hospitality Group Ltd.**


GreenTree Hospitality Group Ltd. ("GreenTree" or the "Company") (NYSE: GHG) is a leading hospitality and restaurant management group in China. As of September 30, 2026, GreenTree had a total number of 4,651 hotels and 203 restaurants. GreenTree was the fourth largest hospitality company in China in 2025 according to the China Hospitality Association. In 2025, HOTELS magazine ranked GreenTree 12th among the 225 largest global hotel groups in terms of number of hotels in its annual HOTELS' 225.


GreenTree has a broad portfolio of diverse brands spanning from the economy to mid-scale, mid-to-up-scale and luxury segments of the hospitality industry mainly in China. Through its strong membership base, expansive booking network, and efficient system, GreenTree aims to keep closer relationships with all of its clients and partners by providing a diverse brand portfolio that features comfort, style and value.
